text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Transformator maker Smit Trafo is unlikely to get a ten million guilder loan from state industrial funds'. (p1)
- Health minister Borst says Liberal leader Bolkestein's intervention in favour of Merck Sharp & Dohme did not affect her drugs policy. (p1)
- Dutch activities of opticians chain Pearle to be taken over by management. (p3)
- Publisher VNU fails to acquire a majority stake in Flemish commercial TV station VTM. (p3)
- Computer chips tester Rood Testhouse's first half net drops to Dfl 780,000 from Dfl 1.1. million in 1995. (p3)
- Builder NBM Amstelland is eyeing Habo unit. (p5)
- Stork Waertsilae Diesel gets a Dfl 100 million loan from EIB to develop new type of Diesel engines. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- 32 people die in Dakota aircrash off Den Helder. (p1)
- Rabobank takes small stake in the Triodos Bank. (p21)
- U.S. temp organisation seeks to take over temp agencies Allround and Interplan. (p21)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Mortgage rate drops below four percent. (p1)
- Kempen & Co.'s new investment fund Orange Midcap fund provers popular with Dfl 210 million of subscriptions. (p37)
- Tour operators angered by low-cost air company EasyJet's new advertising campaign. (p37)
TROUW
- Heir to the throne Prince Willem Alexander opens new ECT container terminal in Rotterdam today. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Social affairs minister Ad Melkert refuses a licence for permanent night shifts at car maker NedCar. (p11)
- IMF expects Dutch economic growth to be lower than Central Planning Bureau's forecasts. (p12)
